candidates.text: Hypothesis: post-resolution origin comparison with a literal-path rebuild is sufficient and minimal when applied to both resolution sites. Prerequisites and permissions: patched copy, loopback servers, permission to run the differential matrix. Bounded test: replace ordinary resolution with a helper that compares resolved origin to base origin; if different, rebuild as base origin plus the supplied text (prefixing one slash when absent); replay the 20-case matrix and the same-origin double-slash control. Expected supporting result: all leaking spellings reach the origin with literal text and the control still preserves its double slash. Falsifier: a leaking spelling still reaching the target or the control collapsing. Cleanup: remove scratch logs and close listeners.

Hypothesis: re-resolving the extracted pathname and search against a dot-anchored base gives literal leading-slash semantics without origin drift, avoiding an explicit origin comparison. Prerequisites and permissions: patched copy, loopback servers and the diagnostics channel. Bounded test: after the ordinary resolution, extract only pathname, search and hash and re-resolve with a base of the form base-origin plus a dot segment; compare resolved origin and path for protocol-relative, triple-slash, backslash and fragment inputs. Expected supporting result: no case routes to the target and dot-segment '/a/../b' still yields '/b'. Falsifier: any target delivery, or a fragment-only input mapping to the wrong path. Cleanup: stop servers and discard scratch trees.

Hypothesis: an allowlist guard in the request constructor that rejects authority-bearing path prefixes is a sufficient single choke point and avoids touching both resolution sites. Prerequisites and permissions: instrumented request constructor, both loopback servers, and permission to run the public forms. Bounded test: reject paths whose prefix denotes an authority and run protocol-relative, absolute, triple-slash, backslash and userinfo inputs plus ordinary controls through the public forms. Expected supporting result: authority forms are rejected and ordinary paths still succeed. Falsifier: an authority form bypassing the guard and reaching the target, or an ordinary control becoming an error. Cleanup: revert instrumentation and stop servers.

Hypothesis: the repaired copy preserves method, body and query normalization for benign inputs and differs from the vulnerable copy only on leaking spellings. Prerequisites and permissions: both copies, the two-server fixture, permission to capture full request lines. Bounded test: send GET with query, POST with a small marker body, HEAD, and a leaking POST through both copies and compare method, request target, Host and body hash at the origin. Expected supporting result: benign cases are byte-equal and leaking cases now land on the origin. Falsifier: any benign case differing beyond ephemeral port digits, or a leaking case still on the target. Cleanup: remove scratch copies and stop servers.
